description:
Move every lock-free lease reader in the commands onto the storage read path and its activeness predicate.

## Background

Four commands read `claims.index.json` directly through `ClaimsIndex::load`, outside the claims lock, each with its own expiry rule:

- `check_active_lease` / `require_active_lease` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:3331-3395`, expiry `:3355-3361`), called from `commands/gate.rs` and `commands/issue.rs`;
- template lease warnings (`commands/template.rs:290-320`, `expires > now` at `:303`), a parallel copy of `captured_lease_warnings` (`commands/mod.rs:741-776`);
- `worktree list` claim counts (`commands/worktree.rs:142-150,252`), whose unit tests build a `ClaimsIndex` by hand (`:550-560,625-635`);
- `validate --leases` (`commands/validate.rs:2488-2505`), which reports expired and orphaned leases and so needs every stored lease (asserted at `tests/cli_item_validate/validation_lease_tests.rs:229,420`).

Storage offers `read_leases`, `read_active_leases`, `read_active_lease` and `Lease::is_active(now)`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `validate --leases` reads through `read_leases`; the other three readers read through the active reads and decide activeness only through `Lease::is_active`. No command calls `ClaimsIndex::load`, and no command compares a lease's expiry or heartbeat itself.
- [hard] REQ-02: Template lease warnings come from the same function as the guarded mutation lease warnings.
- [hard] REQ-03: The worktree unit tests build leases without a `ClaimsIndex`, and the lease-validation CLI tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Lock-free lease readers use the storage read path
